hypotheses.justification: The main proof uses finiteness only through the helper `range_ι_comp_eq_univ` (and `le_iSup_preimage_imagePreimage`, which calls it). Inside that helper the only use is `hWclosed : IsClosed W`, which applies `isClosed_iUnion_of_finite` to W = ⋃ g, (ρ g)⁻¹(U). That fact is only used to get h1 : IsClosed (π '' W). The proof itself shows hπW : π '' W = π '' U without any finiteness. So h1 also follows from `π.isClosedMap _ hUcl` (π is finite, hence universally closed), since U is closed. The rest of the clopen argument needs W to be open (any union of opens is) and its complement to be closed, which is true. Everything else in the main proof works for an arbitrary index type G: the `⨆ g : G` covers, the gluing `existsUnique_gluing'` and `eq_of_locally_eq'`. No other step needs `Fintype G`. So the statement stays true and provable for any group G.

Surjectivity follows from `[IsFinite π]` and `hsec`. A finite morphism is universally closed, so `π.isClosedMap` holds and the range R = π '' univ is closed. Let V : X.Opens be the open complement of R. Then π ⁻¹ᵁ V = ⊥, so Γ(C, π ⁻¹ᵁ V) is terminal and hence subsingleton. The main proof already uses this fact: `CommRingCat.subsingleton_of_isTerminal (C.sheaf.isTerminalOfEqEmpty _)`. By `hsec V`, the map π.app V : Γ(X, V) → Γ(C, π ⁻¹ᵁ V) is injective, so Γ(X, V) is subsingleton too. If V contained a point, Mathlib's instance `Scheme.component_nontrivial` (Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Properties.lean) would make Γ(X, V) nontrivial, which is a contradiction. So V is empty and π.base is surjective. The proof only uses hsurj by passing it to the helper lemmas, so this derived fact can be passed instead. This works with or without `[Finite G]`, so either hypothesis can be deleted on its own.
